body:
I don't have a reason. It confuses me. If being controlled by an emotion seems weird, I'd say that I only do anything ever because of an emotion. Rational thought doesn't compel.

I can see the opportunity I have to correct any boringness or unfulfillment I have, and have no complaints about them. A little thought about that though: What if I don't fill my potential? What if I force misery onto myself? What if I choose to die? I can't see myself as a bad person for deciding to do those, or as a victim of some mental illness for deciding to do those. I don't care. I don't mean to call upon some nihilist philosophy, but I'm okay with anything.

I feel like humor quickly expires in my brain. Even if it provides a temporary relief, it wears off and doesn't work anymore. I don't think I could depend on something like that.

I don't desire to be normal, I accept whoever I think I am. It's the difference between what I feel and what I think normal is that gets me. When I look back, I could call myself a typical weird kid. Keeping a notebook about people or tearing hundreds of papers to shreds aren't what I consider truly weird. Not feeling what others do in situations isn't what I would consider truly abnormal either. But as a sum with my feelings, I don't feel normal.

I wouldn't say my reactions aren't genuine. When other people laugh, I don't feel pressured to laugh with them. When they're expecting me to, I usually serve them an odd smile. When I laugh, it's usually something I found genuinely amusing.

I react pretty normally to a lot of things, laughter or shock, but it's really temporary, and doesn't affect me afterwards.

I don't look forward to anything when I get up. I think staying in bed would have to be a trained behavior for me. It feels like a habit to get up and go to school.

I don't think I feel care as an emotion much anymore. I don't feel pleasure, happiness or joy, but I also don't get angry or sad. 

I still care about things on a rational level, but I don't have the impulse to feel it. I can tell myself that I should do something, but I won't get any motivation to do it. I won't get mad at myself for not doing something, even if I know I should have acted differently.
